newsitem.title: UK: Dated Brent, cash firmer on strong refinery demand.
newsitem.headline: Dated Brent, cash firmer on strong refinery demand.

text.p: Evidence of strong demand for North Sea crude lifted Dated Brent and cash markets on Tuesday although talk was thin ahead of the holiday, traders said.
Feb Brent paper talked at $23.45 a barrel after trading late Monday at $23.25. Intermonth spreads were flat with Feb/Mar valued at +48/+51 cents and Mar/Apr at +52/+56 cents.
Brent CFDs for Dec 30-Jan 3 dates drew support from talk of a firmer differential for a wet deal on Monday.
Traders said a Jan 6-8 cargo fetched Jan Brent -10 cents, three cents more than the previous trade, but both parties declined to comment. Dated Brent was seen strengthening further.
"There's a (Jan) 7-9 cargo on offer at higher numbers today," said a trader.
Five Brent cargoes loading Jan 8-12 were due to be nominated loading dates on Tuesday, traders added.
Other North Sea grades were thinly talked but steady after European and U.S. refiners snapped up at least another six million barrels of spot barrels on Monday to add to the 12 million moved Friday.
Statford traded twice on Monday at stronger premiums, a Jan 19-21 cargo at Dated Brent +41 cents and a Jan 25-27 cargo at +43 cents.

In the Mediterranean, Russian Urals was assessed unchanged at Dated Brent -$1.15 a barrel, basis cif Augusta. A crude pipeline feeding the port of Novorossiisk reopened on Tuesday after a five-day closure for repairs but the port itself stayed shut because of bad weather.

Term customers of Syrian crude were still waiting for state-owned Sytrol to reduce its offer for January Light still further. On Monday, Sytrol offered Dated Brent -18 cents, 31 cents below its opening position but Med refiners insisted the grade was worth no more than Dated -50 cents.
